## Intent

`docs/` gets two things from OKF without becoming a bundle (no
`okf_version`, no `log.md`, no `type`, Diataxis layout kept):

- Per-folder indexes. Each of `docs/tutorials/`, `docs/how-to/`,
  `docs/reference/` and `docs/explanation/` holds a `README.md` listing its
  pages, and `docs/README.md` lists the folders. `check_docs` in
  `src/kmctl/checks.py` checks both levels, the way `check_okf` already does
  for `.okf/` sections. `new_doc` in `src/kmctl/docs.py` adds the entry to
  the folder index (creating it, and its link in `docs/README.md`, with the
  folder), and `scaffold` in `src/kmctl/scaffold.py` writes the new root
  index text.
- Optional front matter on docs pages, using OKF v0.2 names: `description`,
  `stale_after`, `verified`, `sources`. A page may have none. `review_due`
  in `src/kmctl/review_due.py` lists docs pages that carry them, reading
  through `field` in `src/kmctl/okf.py`; `kmctl check` reports a field of the
  wrong shape; `kmctl new doc` writes them by default. Which due reasons
  apply to a docs page and what `new doc` writes by default are the
  operator's call (see report).

Invariant I4 changes, so the ticket adds an ADR with `kmctl new decision`
in `.okf/decisions/` and updates `.okf/manifesto.md`,
`.claude/rules/docs-layout.md`, `docs/reference/commands.md`, the docs page
schemas in `src/kmctl/kinds.py`, the briefing line in `src/kmctl/briefing.py`,
the write-docs skill `apm/.apm/skills/write-docs/SKILL.md`, and this repo's
`docs/`: today 6 pages in 4 folders, 0 folder indexes and 0 pages with
front matter. The migration writes `new:docs/tutorials/README.md`,
`new:docs/how-to/README.md`, `new:docs/reference/README.md` and
`new:docs/explanation/README.md`.

The outcome: on this repo after migration `kmctl check` passes, and in
tests a folder index missing one page gives exactly one finding and a docs
page past its `stale_after` appears in `kmctl review due --json`.

## Could invalidate this plan

- Upgrade path for existing repos. `scaffold` keeps any file that exists,
  so `kmctl update` leaves a downstream repo's flat `docs/README.md` as is
  and writes no folder indexes; the stricter check would then fail every
  pull request in the CI action (`action/knowledge-ci.sh` fails on a failed
  `kmctl check`) until someone migrates by hand. The plan holds only if the
  operator picks a migration rule (see report); without one the change
  breaks every repo already on kmctl.
